request.spec:
Record every change to the sheet in the audit file, one line per change, appended in the order
the changes happen:
PERSON_ADDED name=<name> grade=<grade>, PERSON_EDITED name=<name> grade=<grade>,
CLAIM_ADDED person=<name> amount=<amount> date=<date>, and CLAIM_EDITED with the same fields.
Every line starts with the event, then sheet=<sheet id> and by=<signed-in user>, then the fields
in the order given, separated by single spaces. Amounts are written exactly as the screen shows
them (two decimals) and dates as yyyy-mm-dd. A change that is refused, by any rule now or later,
writes no line and changes nothing.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Record every change to the sheet in the audit file, one line per change, appended in the order
the changes happen:
PERSON_ADDED name=<name> grade=<grade>, PERSON_EDITED name=<name> grade=<grade>,
CLAIM_ADDED person=<name> amount=<amount> date=<date>, and CLAIM_EDITED with the same fields.
Every line starts with the event, then sheet=<sheet id> and by=<signed-in user>, then the fields
in the order given, separated by single spaces. Amounts are written exactly as the screen shows
them (two decimals) and dates as yyyy-mm-dd. A change that is refused, by any rule now or later,
writes no line and changes nothing.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Every add or edit of a person or claim now writes its audit line, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 audit tests on three runs in a row, after one earlier flaky failure that I fixed.

**What changed on the server**
- `Audit.recordOnCommit(...)` writes the line only after the database transaction commits. A refused change (duplicate name, bad amount, unknown row) or one rolled back for any reason, including rules added later, writes nothing.
- `PersonService` writes `PERSON_ADDED` / `PERSON_EDITED ... name=<name> grade=<grade>`. Editing a person didn't pass along the signed-in user before, so `PersonController.update` now passes it through for `by=`.
- `ClaimService` writes `CLAIM_ADDED` / `CLAIM_EDITED ... person=<name> amount=<0.00> date=<yyyy-mm-dd>`. The date is the stored one, so a blank date is logged as the sheet's today.

**A front-end bug I fixed along the way**
The first runs failed now and then, and the cause was there before my change. Setting the sheet's today cleared the people and claims lists and fetched them again. If the test read the rows during that gap, it missed the latest claim and then matched the wrong row as the new one. The server had stored the right data. Now the lists reload only when a sheet is loaded, not when its today changes: there's a new `loaded` signal in `core/sheet.ts`, and `people.ts` watches it.
